data.description:
## Context / Problem

`958e-f4b3-275c-4154` made the write-path drain gate O(1) on a **quiet** store by caching
"nothing can be pending before T" in `.rebar/enrich-gate.json`. The marker is only ever
*written* on a scan that found nothing:

```python
# src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py:374-377
if out:
    _clear_gate_marker(tracker)
else:
    _write_gate_marker(tracker, now_ns, soonest)
```

So a **single** pending entry is enough to disable the fast path for the entire store, and every
subsequent write pays a full walk of every ticket directory until the pending set empties again.

## Measured (2026-08-21, synthetic stores, marker forced cold)

| store size | pending | gate ms |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 1 | 116.9 |
| 1000 | 500 | 157.1 |
| 1000 | 1000 | 206.5 |
| 4000 | 1 | 560.3 |
| 4000 | 500 | 572.3 |
| 4000 | 0 | cold 525.7, **warm 0.110** |

- Cost is **linear in store size** (x4 tickets -> x3.6-4.8) and only weakly sensitive to backlog
  depth (x500 depth -> x1.34; x1000 -> x1.77).
- **Depth 1 already costs the full scan.** The trigger is binary, not proportional.
- The marker, when it engages, is ~4,800x faster (0.110 ms vs 525.7 ms).

On the live 4,938-ticket store this is 1,200-1,330 ms per write.

## Why this is filed separately

Found while debugging `f400-987f-45f6-419a` ("deep enrichment backlog starves late entries").
That bug's mechanism is the **selection order** (an id-sorted prefix); this one is the **marker's
all-or-nothing design**. They share a precondition (a non-empty pending set) but are distinct
mechanisms, proven by the table above: fixing fairness lets *that* store's backlog drain to
empty, which restores the marker there, but it does not help any store that keeps one entry
pending. Folding a marker redesign into a bug fix would exceed that bug's authorised scope, so
it is recorded here instead.

## Scope note (read before implementing)

`958e`'s own block comment (`queue.py:232-254`) enumerates three accepted failure modes and all
three are the marker wrongly saying *quiet*. The branch that never writes the marker at all is
implemented but discussed nowhere — not in the comment, not in the commit message, and not in
any of the 9 marker tests, every one of which seeds a store whose pending set becomes empty.

Note also that story `c1de-d6a0-6cef-4135`'s AC scopes the budget to the quiet case: *"`maybe_drain`
no-ops with no spawn **when nothing soaked**, within `DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS` (20 ms)"*. A gate that
finds a real backlog is not on that no-op path, so this is a **cost/design** improvement, not a
violated contract — size it accordingly.

`f400`'s open question #3 sketches the candidate direction: record "nothing pending BEFORE
index N" rather than all-or-nothing. That is a **design change**, so it wants a plan and a
review, not a drive-by patch.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A store with a standing non-empty pending set does not pay a full store walk on every write.
- [ ] The existing marker honesty rules are preserved: the cache can still only ever say
      "nothing is pending" (never manufacture one), every queue append still invalidates it, and
      it is still TTL-bounded.
- [ ] A test seeds a store with a **permanently non-empty** pending set and pins the gate cost
      (by probe/syscall count, not wall clock — `check_wall_clock_asserts`).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the unit sweep are green.
data.title: enrich gate marker is all-or-nothing: one pending entry disables the O(1) fast path store-wide
